extracted.intended_audience: corporate accountants, registrants, and legal counsel preparing SEC registration statements and Forms 8-K/10-K involving business combinations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on which historical financial statements must be included or updated in SEC registration statements, Form 8‑K filings, and shelf takedowns when a registrant acquires or will acquire businesses (including related-business and aggregate-significance tests). Covers age limits, aggregate/individual significance thresholds, combined vs separate statements, shelf updating, and the S‑X Rule 3‑06 9–12 month substitution rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum age of Rule 3-05 financial statements for an IPO
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registration statement relates to an IPO, the most recent audited financial statements required by Rule 3-05 must not be more than one year and 45 days old at the date the registration statement becomes effective. [S-X Rule 3-12(d)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See chapter 7 for additional information about acquired business financial statements in initial registration statements. S‑X Rule 8‑08 has no similar one-year-plus-45-days requirement; small reporting companies (SRCs) may have different timing (see related guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: SRC filing timing for acquired-business financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: For a business acquired by an SRC, the financial statements for the acquired business may be filed up to 90 days after year-end if the SRC expects to report income in the current year and has reported income in at least one of the two previous years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects that S‑X Rule 8‑08 does not impose the same one-year-and-45-day timing as Rule 3‑12(d) for IPOs. See Question 4.4.120 for additional context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional disclosures when multiple acquisitions are individually insignificant but aggregate >50%
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple acquisitions (individually below thresholds or within the 75‑day grace period) aggregate to more than 50% under any significance test, the registrant must provide pro forma financial information depicting the aggregate impact and must provide financial statements covering at least the most recent fiscal year and most recent interim period for any acquired (or to be acquired) business for which financial statements are not yet required solely because of the 75‑day grace period. [S‑X Rule 3‑05(b)(2)(iv)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The obligation is based on the aggregate significance of acquisitions and probable acquisitions since the registrant’s latest audited fiscal year-end balance sheet. Filing the Form 10‑K results in a fresh start on aggregate measurement; before the 10‑K is filed the measurement period may be up to 15 months depending on filer status. Example scenarios illustrate when pro forma and additional audited/unaudited statements are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate-significance measurement baseline and reset
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate significance of acquisitions (and probable acquisitions) is measured since the registrant’s latest audited fiscal year-end balance sheet; filing the Form 10‑K resets that measurement period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore, acquisitions occurring after the last audited balance sheet are aggregated for the significance tests until the next Form 10‑K is filed, which restarts the measurement period. Early fiscal-year takedowns may therefore be subject to an aggregate measurement period of up to 15 months depending on filer status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shelf registration — age requirements of financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: For shelf (delayed/continuous) offerings, financial statements that meet age requirements at effectiveness may not meet them at time of takedown. After nine months from effectiveness, the audited balance sheet can be no more than 16 months old. [Securities Act §10(a)(3)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Form S‑3 registrants generally incorporate by reference periodic reports (Forms 8‑K, 10‑K, 10‑Q), registration statements for delayed/continuous offerings are often automatically updated as periodic reports are filed. However, care must be taken that the age of audited statements meets takedown timing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a registrant must amend a shelf registration statement (fundamental change)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must amend a shelf registration statement if there is a fundamental change in its business (an S‑K Item 512 undertaking). Whether a business acquisition (completed or probable) is a fundamental change is a legal determination for management (with counsel) to make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a fundamental change has occurred, the registrant updates the shelf registration by filing a post-effective amendment. In many cases, filing the acquired business’s financial statements on a Form 8‑K (and incorporating by reference) satisfies the updating requirements without filing an amended registration statement. Management should consider quantitative and qualitative significance and probability of consummation when assessing fundamental change. Typically, acquisitions or groups of acquisitions less than 50% significance do not represent a fundamental change.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC staff expectations for updating shelf registration when individual acquisition ≥50%
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC staff expects shelf registration statements to be updated for completed acquisitions that are individually at or above 50% significance, regardless of whether they constitute a formal fundamental change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a completed acquisition above 50% does not, by itself, legally equal a fundamental change, the staff expects the registration to be updated (e.g., by filing the Rule 3‑05 financial statements). See FRM 2045.3 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating shelf registration for probable >50% acquisitions (timing and exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a probable acquisition exceeds 50% significance at time of takedown, the takedown may proceed without providing Rule 3‑05 financial statements unless management determines the probable acquisition constitutes a fundamental change. If the acquisition is completed before the takedown and exceeds 50%, the registrant must file the target’s financial statements prior to the takedown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is an exception for offerings and sales that are not for the purpose of capital raising — such transactions may proceed without providing Rule 3‑05 financial statements when the acquisition does not represent a fundamental change. See Questions 4.4.280 and related examples (e.g., Example 4.4.140).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K use to satisfy updating requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant can satisfy the requirement to file/update financial statements for an acquired (or to‑be‑acquired) business by filing those financial statements on a Form 8‑K instead of filing an amended registration statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 8‑K does not require filing financial statements for probable acquisitions or individually insignificant acquisitions; however, if such transactions are a fundamental change, the registrant can update a shelf by filing a Form 8‑K with the target’s historical financial statements. Filing on Form 8‑K is commonly used to incorporate financials by reference into a Form S‑3 shelf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospectus supplement / post-effective amendment timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A prospectus supplement (Rule 424(c)) or post‑effective amendment is required if the prospectus is in use beyond nine months after effectiveness or if the audited balance sheet is more than 16 months old.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post‑effective amendments to continuous or delayed registration statements are generally considered new filings and thus require compliance with S‑X Rule 3‑12 or 8‑08 on the effective date. Amending a registration statement solely to provide an exhibit does not amend the prospectus. See FRM 1220.6 and FRM 1220.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial-statement requirements for acquisition of related businesses (cumulative testing)
rubrics_metrics.description: For acquisitions of related businesses, significance is determined based on their combined (as‑if combined) financial information. If the cumulative significance of the group requires a Form 8‑K, the Rule 3‑05 financial statements required are those of the individual (or combined) businesses included in the tested group, but only to the extent those statements have not previously been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tested group includes both probable and consummated acquisitions that are related. When the aggregate test is significant, a registrant must include the financial statements of each individual (or combined) business in the tested group (even if individually insignificant), for the periods indicated by the cumulative significance tests. Examples illustrate the required periods and how they change as the cumulative significance increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K vs registration-statement scope for related businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: If related-business testing is significant: for a Form 8‑K, include each related business for which the acquisition has been consummated (if those financial statements have not been previously filed); for a registration statement, include each related business for which the acquisition has been consummated or is probable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction reflects the different purposes and timing of a Form 8‑K (disclosing completed events) versus a registration statement (which must show probable transactions that affect investor decisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined financial statements rules for related businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Combined financial statements may be presented only where some or all entities are under common control or common management; otherwise combined financial statements are not appropriate, even though significance is tested using as‑if combined information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If combined financial statements are inappropriate or a registrant elects not to present them, separate financial statements must be provided for each related business for the periods required by the combined significance tests. Combined statements (if used) must cover any period for which the businesses are under common control/management for the entire period. See section 9.3 of KPMG Handbook for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: S‑X Rule 3-06 — substituting 9–12 months for a one-year audited period
rubrics_metrics.description: S‑X Rule 3‑06 permits filing audited financial statements covering a period of nine to twelve months to satisfy a one‑year requirement in limited circumstances: (a)(1) the issuer changed its fiscal year; (a)(2) the issuer made a significant business acquisition for which Rule 3‑05/3‑14/8‑04/8‑06 financials are required and the interim audited period pertains to the business being acquired; or (a)(3) the Commission so permits. [S‑X Rule 3‑06]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule is commonly used when an acquired business lacks full‑year audited statements and provides flexibility in selecting a 9–12 month audited period. The exception is available to all registrants (including SRCs) but may not be applied outside these situations without written SEC staff permission. S‑X Rule 3‑06 may not be used to satisfy target-company financial statement requirements in a proxy or Form S‑4 because those are not provided pursuant to Rule 3‑05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations when multiple years of audited financials are required (application of Rule 3-06)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where more than one fiscal year is required, S‑X Rule 3‑06 may be relied upon for only one of the required fiscal years. For instance, when two years of audited financial statements are required, registrants may provide one year as a 9–12 month audited period and the other year as a full fiscal year. The audited periods should be contiguous (no gap between audited periods). [S‑X Rule 3‑06(b)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants may choose which fiscal year to satisfy with a 9–12 month audited period, but the chosen period must be audited and should immediately precede or follow the full fiscal year provided. Examples (4.5.40–4.5.50) illustrate alternative acceptable combinations and the need to provide any required unaudited interim information when shorter audited periods are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and updating of interim periods when using shortened audited periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of a 9–12 month audited period can create a need to provide unaudited interim financial information for subsequent periods. If a registrant provides an audited period that ends earlier than the registrant’s filing date, it may need to provide unaudited interim statements covering the intervening period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show that providing audited statements as of a September 30 period may require unaudited interim information through the registrant’s filing date. When cumulative significance tests increase after initial filings, registrants must consider whether updated interim financial statements are needed for previously filed related businesses (dynamic updating requirement).
